newsitem.title: UK: UK water customer lobby calls for cuts in bills.
newsitem.headline: UK water customer lobby calls for cuts in bills.

text.p: A British water consumers lobby group called on watchdog Ofwat to cut bills at its next price review in 1999 on Tuesday.

"We look to (Ofwat head Ian Byatt) to take the toughest action possible...to reduce the companies' price limits in 1999. Customers want to see an immediate and substantial cut in averge water bills and bills thereafter kept below the rate of inflation," Jim Gardner, chairman of Ofwat's National Customer Council (ONCC), said in a statement.

The ONCC added that it felt it would be "unhelpful" if the Environment Agency just produced a list of expensive options for improvement "without regard to affordability and to which no priorities are attached."
The ONCC is also calling for all customers to be entitled to compensatory payments when supplies are interrupted, even during droughts.
Gardner said European Union directives on quality and environmental standards would have to be based on "sound science, costs and benefits...and an appropriate timescale."
The ONCC also said that Byatt has recommended to the government that the council should become a statutory body.
Byatt will step down as a member of the ONCC.
